title: Invocation Heuristic Evaluator for Tool Selection & Arg Validation
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Build an offline evaluation harness that measures how configuration or model changes affect tool/function selection accuracy and argument validation fidelity.

This harness will run nightly against canary model/config snapshots and produce deterministic metrics and diff reports that feed our alerting and rollback automation. The goal is early detection of regressions introduced by model updates, tokenizer changes, or runtime routing logic tweaks.
goals: Detect tool selection accuracy regressions (drop in top-1 accuracy or increase in ambiguous selection rate).
Verify argument schema adherence and sanitization rate for invoked functions across config variants.
Provide actionable diffs (request examples, model responses, chosen function + args) surfaced in Console and as alerts tied to commits/rollouts.
Integrate with canary rollout pipeline to block or annotate releases when thresholds are breached.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end in CI/nightly and publishes metrics to the Invocation QA dashboard.
Defines and computes at least three selection metrics: top-1 accuracy, top-3 overlap, and selection confidence distribution.
Argument validation metrics implemented: schema pass-rate, sanitized-arg rate, and malformed-arg false-positive rate.
Regression detection rule set implemented: configurable thresholds and a diff exporter that includes 50 representative failing examples.
Alerting: breaches trigger both a Console incident card and a Slack channel message with links to failing examples and the responsible commit.
technical_approach: Dataset: assemble a stable eval set composed of customer-derivative prompts, public QA pairs, and synthetically-perturbed prompts to probe edge cases.
Simulate rollout variants by running the same inputs against baseline and candidate model/config pairs; compare tool selection and args.
Scoring: implement deterministic comparators for selection alignment (string-normalized function keys) and arg semantic equality (schema-aware comparators that ignore ordering where appropriate).
Perturbations: include input truncation, prompt template variance, temperature/stochasticity sweeps, and tokenization shifts to catch brittle heuristics.
Sanitization checks: validate arguments against OpenAPI-like schemas and our runtime sanitizer rules; flag silent corrections and lossy truncations.
Reporting: produce per-test diffs, aggregate histograms, and time-series metrics sent to our telemetry backend; export an S3 artifact with failing examples and anonymized payloads.
Integration: wire the harness to the canary pipeline (runtime-1.21) so the CI job returns non-zero when P0-level thresholds are crossed.
testing_plan: Unit tests for comparator logic (schema matcher, canonicalization rules).
E2E job that runs on PRs touching invocation routing, kernel selection, or sanitizer codepaths.
Nightly runs against a pinned baseline model and the latest candidate; collect historical baselines for trend analysis.
Manual review workflow for first 50 flagged diffs to reduce false positives and iterate on comparator heuristics.
